hero.line: Where fire is the only author.
hero.sub: Iron-rich earth, pine wood fire, and stilled time. A Song Dynasty lineage capturing fleeting constellations in dark glaze.

soul.body: Jianzhan is more than a tea bowl; it is an encounter between earth and cosmic chance. Thrown by hand and fired in ancient dragon kilns, one clay enters the kiln, yet ten thousand colours emerge. What the flame decides, the artisan accepts.
soul.caption: Glaze detail — iron crystals on a black ground

collection.title: Selected Works
collection.note: Each vessel is a singular occurrence — glazes born from momentary alignments of heat, draft, and mineral ash that human hands cannot replicate.

craft.title: Passed down through generations
craft.body: Our artisans preserve Song-era methods, firing unrefined minerals in wood-fuelled kilns. Nothing is hurried: forming, drying, glazing, and days inside the fire are entirely surrendered to the patient rhythm of the kiln.

gifting.title: A quiet object, kept for a lifetime
gifting.body: Each piece arrives linen-wrapped with a recorded firing note — the year, the kiln and the conditions of its making. Suitable for a collector’s shelf, a tea table, or a gift that outlives the occasion.
list: Firing note signed by the studio
Care card with use and washing guidance

closing.body: The kiln does not bend to human will. We merely shape the clay; nature finishes the glaze.
